answer: A cheap identity is a nebula of throwaway accounts: countless, diffuse, nearly free to spawn. So make each identity costly to create and costly to lose: require a small stake bonded per account plus a proof-of-work or credential tied to a real device or reputation history. The bond is slashed on fraud, so an attacker pays per sockpuppet. Then let trust spread by whisper: signed actions and peer attestations build a graph where new identities start near zero weight and earn influence only through sustained, checkable work. One fake signal is cheap; a thousand must each pay the stake.
